title: Direct Observation of the Hydrated Active and Degraded Structures of Cu-Exchanged Zeolite Catalysts using Electron Ptychography
content: Cu-SSZ-13 (CHA-type) zeolite is widely used as a catalyst for neutralizing NOx in exhaust gases from diesel engine vehicles. While Cu-SSZ-13 exhibits high catalytic activity, H-SSZ-13 (without Cu) has only limited activity, suggesting that Cu-containing moieties serve as active sites. Therefore, it is important to understand the position and properties of Cu ion within the CHA framework. However, experimental methods for analyzing the surface structure of active sites are currently unavailable, and structural analyses have been limited to bulk-averaged measurements. It has been reported that the position of Cu shifts in the presence of water in operating conditions. However, the position shows inconsistencies between various X-ray experimental methods and previous studies based on DFT calculations [1-2], preventing a comprehensive discussion of the active structure under hydrated conditions. In this study, we employed electron ptychography, which enables atomic-resolution imaging under low electron dose conditions [3], to visualize Cu site displacements in Cu-SSZ-13 due to hydration and dehydration. Furthermore, we compared the observed hydrated structures with those reported in previous research. Additionally, by analyzing the Cu positions and hydration states in both degraded CHA-type and AEI-type zeolites (with superior durability) before and after degradation, we investigated the coordination states of Cu species responsible for catalytic activity.
